purpose: Refine the public parameter funnel after verification of the exact q-Horn deletion dependence and add backdoor-DNF structure before any new JANUS mechanism is designed.

q_horn_deletion_update.old_map_status: FPT known; polynomial promotion rule intentionally left unresolved pending explicit parameter dependence.

verified_later_exact_result.result: Deletion q-Horn Backdoor Set Detection admits an exact FPT algorithm via 3-Skew-Symmetric Multicut.
verified_later_exact_result.parameter: k = size of a smallest deletion q-Horn backdoor set
verified_later_exact_result.reference: M. S. Ramanujan and Saket Saurabh, Linear Time Parameterized Algorithms via Skew-Symmetric Multicuts, SODA 2014, DOI 10.1137/1.9781611973402.126

polynomial_promotion.derivation: For k <= c log n, 12^k <= n^(c log 12), and k^5 contributes only a polylogarithmic factor.
polynomial_promotion.note: This supersedes the older STACS 2013 approximation-based SAT bound 2^O(k^2)*ell*n for purposes of the universal coverage map.

q_horn_deletion_update.important_distinction: Strong/weak q-Horn backdoor detection is W[2]-hard in the STACS 2013 result; the tractable exact route here is deletion distance to q-Horn.

backdoor_depth_update.verified_result: Backdoor-depth detection admits FPT approximation for these Schaefer classes, and CNF-SAT is linear-time on bounded-depth formulas.
backdoor_depth_update.strictness: Bounded ordinary backdoor size implies bounded backdoor depth, but there are formulas of constant backdoor depth and arbitrarily large ordinary backdoor size.
backdoor_depth_update.reference: Jan Dreier, Sebastian Ordyniak, Stefan Szeider, SAT backdoors: Depth beats size, JCSS 142 (2024), DOI 10.1016/j.jcss.2024.103520
backdoor_depth_update.coverage_firewall: Constant bounded depth is an established polynomial lane. Any growing-depth-to-polynomial promotion must use the explicit f(k) dependence of the imported detector/solver rather than assuming O(log n) automatically suffices.

new_public_door.name: BACKDOOR_DNF
new_public_door.definition_summary: A tautological DNF over backdoor variables where each term, viewed as a partial assignment, moves the CNF into a tractable base class.
verified_results: Detection is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number of DNF terms for Horn, AntiHorn/dual-Horn, and 2CNF under the theorem-supported combinations.
The algorithm also supports heterogeneous Horn+2CNF and AntiHorn+2CNF cases described by the paper.
Backdoor DNFs can be strictly more compact than ordinary backdoor sets and backdoor trees.
references: Sebastian Ordyniak, Andre Schidler, Stefan Szeider, Backdoor DNFs, JCSS 144 (2024), DOI 10.1016/j.jcss.2024.103547
new_public_door.why_it_matters_for_R50G25X: Large Horn/Krom deletion backdoor size does not rule out a small DNF of partial assignments routing different branches into tractable classes.
new_public_door.firewall: Do not assume a logarithmic number of DNF terms is polynomial coverage until the exact imported f(t) detector/solver dependence is frozen. Constant t is sufficient for polynomial coverage.

revised_killer_pass_order.reason: Polynomial direct decomposition; cheapest new exact screen and may discharge clauses before parameter tests.
Polynomial direct P-lane; run before any FPT search.
Ordinary backdoor size can be arbitrarily large at constant depth; therefore current large deletion sets do not screen this route.
Exact FPT detector exists with O(12^k*k^5*ell); k=O(log n) is now a formally valid polynomial promotion condition.
Can be more compact than sets/trees and may route different partial assignments to different public P classes.
Strong orthogonal structural route, but decomposition search/DP is heavier than direct polynomial screens.

intersection_rule: Only frozen residuals surviving all applicable public direct and parameterized doors become candidates for a new Universal Residual Funnel mechanism.
anti_overclaim: FPT does not imply polynomial for a growing parameter without explicit f(k).
A finite residual surviving a bounded parameter threshold is not an asymptotic lower bound.
Failure of one backdoor representation does not imply failure of depth, DNF, heterogeneous, q-Horn, or width routes.
No finite rescreen proves hardness or P!=NP.
No public-lane success on a finite corpus proves universal SAT in P.
